trajectory.first_user_message:
As an optimization and mathematical modeling expert in a shared bike service company, every night, you need to rebalance the bikes among the stations in your responsible region. So the basic information is that you can control several rebalancing vehicles (`vehicle_count`). The vehicles can start driving from the depot, reach stations in your region, pick up/drop off bikes at the stations, and then return to the depot. Rebalancing vehicles share the same capacity (how many bikes they can handle at the same time, `vehicle_capacity`), and the same depot (`depot`). You know the coordinates of the depot and the stations (`latitude` and `longitude`), and the distances between any two coordinates are computed as the great circle distances in miles.

skills.name: logistics-rules-to-optimization
skills.heading: Logistics Rules To Optimization
skills.diagnosis: The bike-rebalancing task requires careful translation of inventory-flow, routing, and unmet-demand penalties into a strong optimization formulation. The near-optimal but failing result suggests the formulation may have been correct yet too weak or overly loose, especially around linking service quantities to visits, unmet-demand modeling, and load propagation. Weak formulations can materially reduce incumbent quality within fixed solve limits.
skills.repair_instruction: Expand the skill with stronger formulation patterns for bike-rebalancing and inventory-routing problems: explicit pickup/dropoff variables linked to visit binaries with tight bounds; stronger vehicle load propagation constraints; absolute-deviation or positive/negative slack formulations for unmet targets; guidance on avoiding weak big-M constants; valid inequalities for global balance and capacity feasibility; and recommendations for balancing travel cost versus unmet-demand penalties. Include a subsection on formulation strength and solver performance impacts.

skills.name: routing-subtour-elimination
skills.heading: Routing Subtour Elimination
skills.diagnosis: No subtour violations occurred, but routing-connectivity formulation strength still likely affected search performance and incumbent quality. Basic subtour elimination approaches such as plain MTZ can leave weak LP relaxations, slowing progress toward high-quality incumbents in multi-vehicle inventory-routing problems.
skills.repair_instruction: Enhance the skill with performance-oriented connectivity guidance for VRP-style MIPs. Compare MTZ against flow-based and cutset formulations, recommend stronger connectivity constraints for small-to-medium routing problems, explain how subtour elimination interacts with capacity/load propagation, and add symmetry-breaking and depot-reachability strengthening techniques that improve incumbent quality under limited solve time.

skills.name: scip-opt
skills.heading: SCIP Optimization
skills.diagnosis: The solution quality failure points to insufficient guidance on obtaining strong incumbents for routing-style MIPs under time limits. Existing guidance emphasizes building and solving correct models but under-specifies practical incumbent-improvement strategies such as parameter tuning, warm starts, primal heuristics, formulation strengthening, symmetry reduction, and post-solve improvement loops. The produced model was feasible but likely not optimized aggressively enough to close the small benchmark gap.
skills.repair_instruction: Add a dedicated section on benchmark-competitive SCIP usage for routing and inventory-routing MIPs. Include recommended parameter tuning for heuristics, cuts, presolve, separation, and time/gap management; explain how to build and inject greedy or repair-based MIP starts; describe incumbent-polishing and local-improvement workflows; add guidance on tightening bounds and adding valid inequalities; and include troubleshooting advice for cases where the solver stalls with feasible but weak incumbents.
